subject: kbox running ghcr.io/kense-labs/dsh-acp:latest (dsh-acp ACP agent) on macOS arm64 / HVF

cold_rootfs_assembly.description: OCI 7 layers -> guest-native ext4 (4.0 GiB sparse, ~780 MB actual) + sparse_sha256 hashing
cold_rootfs_assembly.note: first boot per isolated K_HOME only; cached afterwards. debug/unoptimized hashing is ~2.8x slower than release.

vm_boot.description: VM process spawn -> exec server heartbeat -> VM ready (historical detailed log)

model_turn.note: LLM/network dominated; kbox ACP overhead (~19 ms) is <2% of a prompt turn.

host_resources.note: CPU spikes to ~100% of one core occur only during cold ext4 assembly; steady-state control-plane CPU is near idle.

conclusion: kbox adds ~20 ms per warm ACP session and ~1.3 s of VM boot; the dominant one-off cost is ~76 s cold ext4 rootfs assembly per new K_HOME. Steady-state runtime cost is dominated by the DeepSeek API (~0.7-1.7 s per prompt), not by kbox.
